To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most common algorithms are wave and credit-recovery algorithms; the most common communication protocols are synchronous and FIFO; the most common network topologies are tree and ring; the most common algorithm symmetry is asymmetric; and the most common required process knowledge is that of a process's local state and its knowledge of its immediate neighbors.

there are four basic algorithm types: wave, credit-recovering, token-based, and state-based; that all algorithms require a connected, synchronous communication network; that the algorithms are symmetric; that the algorithms require knowledge of the number of processes; that the algorithms use the synchronous communication protocol; that the algorithms assume FIFO channels; that the algorithms do not optimize the number of messages sent; and that the algorithms are fault tolerant.

the following are true: (1) the algorithms can be classified by algorithm type, required network topology, and required knowledge; (2) all algorithms require knowledge of the system; (3) all algorithms are either wave or credit-recovery type algorithms; (4) the algorithms require either a synchronous or asynchronous communication protocol; (5) all algorithms require a FIFO channel; and (6) all algorithms are fault-tolerant.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the most popular DTD algorithm is the one that uses a wave to propagate termination information throughout the network.
the majority of DTD algorithms can be categorized into one of two types: wave algorithms and credit-recovery algorithms, with a subset of these falling under the category of wave-credit recovery.
there is a large variety of DTD algorithms, but most of them can be classified into one of the categories we propose.
